title: Orchestration lane-fold: context-aware sidebar zoning and progressive routing
creator: Asha Mehta
description: Problem: The current left rail is overloaded: quick shortcuts, project nav, rollout controls and cost lenses compete for space and push users into deep flows to reach common actions. This ticket scopes a design pattern we call the 'orchestration lane-fold' — a context-aware, multi-zoned sidebar that compresses low-priority surfaces and exposes task‑relevant lanes (Deployments, Cost, Observability, Shortcuts) based on route context and user role. Goals: reduce click depth for common workflows, make rollouts and cost signals discoverable without noise, and provide predictable routing rules for engineering to implement. Deliverables: hi-fi Figma prototype for desktop and narrow tablet, annotated interaction spec, acceptance criteria and a small moderated usability run (8–10 engineers/PMs).
acceptance_criteria: Primary nav items remain accessible within 2 clicks from homepage
Rollout controls (canary, rollback) surface in lane header when viewing a model or deployment route
Cost lens summary becomes a pinned mini-widget in billing-heavy workspaces and reflects per-route token breakdowns
Compact mode compresses lower-priority lanes but retains affordances for quick-jump via keyboard shortcuts
Engineering can implement routing decisions via a single feature flag and config-driven lane rules
prototyping_notes: Built two compression modes: Persistent (user toggles) and Contextual (auto-compress based on route)
Implemented progressive reveal on hover for narrow screens to avoid layout shift
Introduced lane headers that advertise stateful controls (e.g., 'Canary: 10% — Promote / Rollback')
Keyboard-driven quick-jump: 'G' then lane letter opens lane directly — included in prototype
usability_findings: (02-12) Engineers found rollout controls 40% faster to reach in context vs baseline
(02-14) Two PMs confused the mini cost widget state when there were concurrent rollout errors — need clearer error affordance
(02-20) Observability lane should expose recent traces count; users expect one-click to open trace view
(03-02) Accessibility: compressed lanes need a persistent focus ring and aria-expanded labels for screen readers
engineering_notes: Suggested implementation: feature-flagged lane rules (yaml) evaluated in routing layer; front-end consumes lane metadata via /config/ui-lanes endpoint
Performance: avoid server roundtrip for contextual compression on route-change — compute client-side using route -> lane map cached at bootstrap
Backend: cost widget will need a small aggregated endpoint (billing/route-summary) scoped to team and model; ENG-22011 tracked separately
Migration: keep legacy sidebar routes behind flag to enable staged rollouts to <10% orgs
decisions: Decided to prioritize desktop first; narrow-tablet support will be lighter weight (no persistent lane headers)
Keep workspace switcher separate from lane-fold; add a compact workspace chip in the top-left rather than migrating it into lanes
Rollout controls are surfaced only when route context includes a deployment_id to avoid clutter on non-deploy pages
Cost mini-widget will show 3 metrics (tokens, estimated $/hr, largest consumer) to balance signal vs noise
